# Plan one: the four repositories and every move of section 6

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task by task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Build, outside iCloud, the working trees of the four repositories of spec section 2 and make every move of spec section 6, so that the owner commits and pushes: `metis-app`, whose 13 checks pass with the app folder as its root and whose brand files and wireframe manifest come from pinned copies that `docs.lock` locks by hash; `metis-docs`, which holds every English page of spec 3.1 except `site/` and `mcp/` (plan three), passes every check of spec 3.6 in a pull-request workflow, and lists its current pages in a generated `llms.txt`; `metis-backend` and `metis-infra`, which start with their instruction files.

**Architecture:** Each repository is a fresh `git init -b main` working tree under `~/metis-run/repos/` (R1), filled by copying from today's folder, which stays read-only (R2). Two lanes run first and may run in parallel: the app lane (Tasks 1 to 5: copy, pinned copies, path switches, every check) and the documents lane (Tasks 6 to 9: copy, BRD build and wireframe builder moved, the checks of 3.6 as `tools/` with tests, the entry pages). Content waves follow, written by subagents from the sources this plan names (Tasks 10 to 13: decision records, business, design, architecture, components, operations), and only then the translation of the records into `history/` (Task 14), as spec 6.2 orders. Task 15 closes `metis-docs` (code owners, `llms.txt`, every check and oracle clean), Task 16 writes `metis-backend` and `metis-infra`, Task 17 records the run, and Task 18 is the owner's commit and push. Migration-only tools (the translation check, the page oracles, the edit scripts) live in `~/metis-run/repos-tools/`, outside every repository, because the originals they compare stay in the owner's private store.

**Tech Stack:** Node 24.15.0 and `node --test`; pnpm 11.28.4 and the app's unchanged toolchain (Expo SDK 57, TypeScript 6, Jest 29, StrykerJS 10, Playwright 1.63, Maestro); Python 3 standard library (BRD Markdown); pandoc, LibreOffice and poppler (BRD Word edition, on demand only); gitleaks 8.30.1; GitHub Actions `actions/checkout@v7` and `actions/setup-node@v7`.

**Spec:** `spec/2026-10-11-repos-and-docs-design.md` (approved: RD-01 to RD-12, sections 1 to 6). Brief: `.superpowers/repos/writer-prompt.md` (scope of plan one, controller rulings R1 to R12, owner steps).

## Global Constraints

- **R2, today's folder is read-only.** `/Users/mrpo/projects/metis` is copied from, never moved, deleted or edited, except this plan (as-built notes), the spec's status line and the ledgers under `.superpowers/`. Everything that stays outside every repository simply stays there: it is the owner's private store of spec 6.1. `git ls-files` there is a read; no other git command runs there.
- **R1, no commit.** Never run `git add`, `git commit` or `git push`, anywhere. `git init -b main` runs once per working tree in `~/metis-run/repos/<name>`. Every "commit" of the template is "record the changed files in the task's ledger"; the owner commits and pushes in Task 18.
- **Owner steps stop the run.** Creating or choosing the GitHub organization, creating the four repositories and the teams, adding remotes, committing, pushing and installing anything on GitHub are the owner's (marked OWNER STEP). The executor asks and waits only where a step needs the answer.
- **English, ASCII letters, no dash.** Every file of `metis-docs` is English (RD-04): no letter outside ASCII except on the line after a `lang-exception:` line, and no em dash or en dash anywhere; this plan and every code block obey the same rule (escapes such as `\u2013` stand for the characters).
- **FE-27.** Code, comments, test titles, lint messages and tool output in English; a comment gives the reason, never a ruling id or a line number; tests read their values from fixtures and constants, never retype them.
- **FE-18.** Install a tool only when an approved spec item needs it, prove the need with the error line, record it in the ledger. Measured while writing: gitleaks (spec 3.6) was missing (`command not found: gitleaks`) and was installed with Homebrew.
- **R11 and FE-26, heavy work.** One heavy job at a time: the full `pnpm verify` of Task 5 (about 2 h 15 min, of which mutation testing is most), `pnpm canary all` (7 to 8.5 min), a BRD Word build. Never run Jest while Stryker runs. `pnpm verify` and `pnpm canary` lower their own priority. Run them in `~/metis-run/repos/metis-app`, outside iCloud.
- **RTK traps** (CLAUDE.md): compare files with `cmp`, `shasum` or `diff -u`, never a bare `diff`; use `rtk proxy find`, `rtk proxy ls -a`, `rtk proxy pnpm exec jest`, and `rtk proxy node --test --test-reporter=tap <file>` when a TAP summary must show. Measured by the pre-flight scan (ruling C19): the hook also rewrites `head -N <file>`, a plain `grep <pattern> <file>` and `grep -n`; read lines of a file with `sed -n` and search a file with `grep -E`.
- **Clients stay separate (ruling C16, workspace rule).** No file written or copied into the four repositories names another project of the owner's workspace. Brand files that credit one get neutral wording; the oracle reads the names from `~/metis-run/repos-tools/other-projects.txt`, written at run time from the other top-level folders of `~/projects` (all but metis, pdev, ssh-keys), so no repository file ever holds them: `grep -rliE -f ~/metis-run/repos-tools/other-projects.txt ~/metis-run/repos --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git` prints nothing.
- **The GitHub account (owner, 11 Oct 2026; ruling C1 revised).** The four repositories are private repositories of the personal account `phongnguyen6691`, reached through the SSH alias `github-phong` (probe: `Hi phongnguyen6691!`). The `gh` CLI of this Mac is logged in as another account: no step uses `gh`.
- **Rulings C14 to C28** (the pre-flight scan, ledger `progress.md`) bind every task they name; the controller carries each into its task's dispatch.
- **R12, free only.** Nothing in plan one needs a paid service or a paid GitHub feature; `.github/CODEOWNERS` is written now and takes effect when the organization moves to GitHub Team (spec 3.7, 4.9).
- **Never cut an approved item (FE-23).** Anything of the spec this plan cannot do is in "Open questions" with its reason; anything found missing while running leads the ledger's report to the owner.

## Review Focus

1. **The pinned copies.** `metis-app` reads the brand files and the wireframe manifest only from `pinned/` (eight files read outside the app today, not six: W1); a byte changed in a copy, a copy missing or a file not in `docs.lock` turns `gate:tooling` red; the copies equal the `metis-docs` files at the end (oracle `pins`).
2. **The BRD is unchanged.** Moved into `metis-docs` and built without `sips`, both Markdown editions equal today's committed editions plus only the page header, hyphens for en dashes, and three path rewrites (proven byte for byte, W11, W12).
3. **Records stay records.** Every translation keeps its original line for line (the translation check), every record opens with a banner generated from `history/records.json`, and no record is current truth (`llms.txt` lists them under Optional).
4. **Pages tell the truth (R5, R6).** A module page carries every requirement id of its module and says what users can do today (for 22 of 23 modules: nothing yet); a page about a planned part is a draft whose first line says so; no price, cost or legal-entity comparison anywhere (R9).
5. **CI at the new roots.** `metis-app`'s workflow names no `apps/metis`; `metis-docs`'s workflow runs the tools' own tests, every check and a pinned, hash-checked gitleaks, with no paid action.

## How to run

- **Ledger:** `/Users/mrpo/projects/metis/.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-11-repos-and-moves/progress.md` (a ledger, so R2 allows it): one line `Task N: complete` per finished task, the commands run with their measured output, and every ruling taken while running. Per repository, `changed-files-<repository>.txt` beside it, written in Task 17.
- **Working trees:** `~/metis-run/repos/metis-app`, `metis-docs`, `metis-backend`, `metis-infra` (R1). **Migration tools:** `~/metis-run/repos-tools/` (never committed).
- **Order:** Task 0, then the app lane (1 to 5) and the documents lane (6 to 9), which share nothing and may run in parallel; Task 5's heavy run waits until no other heavy job runs. Tasks 10 to 13 need Tasks 6 to 9; they fan out to subagents by page group, which write different files. Task 14 starts only when Tasks 10 to 13 are reviewed (spec 6.2: lasting content first, then the translations). Then 15, 16, 17, 18.
- **Subagents:** one implementer and one reviewer per task, as in the earlier plans; content tasks dispatch one subagent per page group and translations one subagent per record or chunk (Task 14 gives the brief). Every subagent prompt carries the Global Constraints above and the writing rules of `metis-docs/AGENTS.md` (Task 9). Only the controller runs `node tools/generate.mjs`, because it rewrites `llms.txt` and the banners.
- **Oracles:** every step ends with a command and its expected output. A content task's oracle is `node tools/check.mjs` filtered to its paths (expected: no line) plus the page-specific rule of `page-oracles.mjs` (expected: `oracle <rule>: clean`).

## Controller rulings (from the brief, recorded as given)

- **R1** Working trees: build each repository in `~/metis-run/repos/<name>` (outside iCloud), created with `git init -b main`; never `git add`, `commit` or `push`; every "commit" step becomes a record of the changed files in the task's ledger; the owner commits and pushes at the end.
- **R2** Today's folder is read-only during execution, except this plan, the spec's status line and `.superpowers/` ledgers; what stays outside every repository stays there as the owner's private store.
- **R3** Pinned copies in `metis-app` mirror `metis-docs` paths under `pinned/` and hold only the files the app reads; `docs.lock` lists the source repository, the source commit and the sha256 of every pinned file; until plan two's bot runs, the commit field says that no commit exists yet; the hashes alone decide the check.
- **R4** No pinned copy in `metis-backend` yet.
- **R5** Pages about parts not built yet are true about being unbuilt: a module page says what users can do today; an architecture or component page about a planned part carries `status: draft` and says in its first line that the part is planned, not built. How `llms.txt` lists draft pages is decided in W21.
- **R6** Module pages carry in their header `ids` every BRD requirement id of their module, taken from the BRD source.
- **R7** The Vietnamese records (27 files marked VI in the inventory, minus `brand/style-guide.md` and `apps/metis-rn-guide.html`, which are rewritten) are translated by machine, one file per subagent, with the banner line of 6.2, no human review, under a mechanical check; the 11 files marked "EN-with-VI-passages" get only their Vietnamese passages translated; the 850 KB plan is chunked (W23).
- **R8** Before the translations, this plan lists the decision records and current pages that carry the lasting content of those records: section "Decision records" and the page specifications.
- **R9** Architecture pages and decision records rewritten from the pitch material hold no price, no cost and no legal-entity comparison (RD-02).
- **R10** Content tasks give, for each page: path, header values, required sections, sources and the oracle.
- **R11** Every oracle is mechanical; heavy runs follow the environment traps.
- **R12** Free only.

## Writer rulings (taken while writing, each with its evidence)

- **W1 Eight files read outside the app, not six.** Spec 6.3 names six. Resolving every relative path literal of the 410 app files found two more: `e2e/web/brand.spec.ts` (the wordmark SVG and the 180 px icon, lines 121 to 123 and 143) and `e2e/web/support.ts` (the tokens, line 19). Both switch to the pinned copies; the four tests that name the old paths (`verify.tree.test.mjs`, `verify.cli.test.mjs`, `check-language.test.mjs`, `e2e/web/support.spec.ts`) change with them.
- **W2 The check of 4.4 lives in `gate:tooling`.** `scripts/pinned.mjs` and its test compare every copy under `pinned/` with `docs.lock`, so `pnpm verify` keeps its 13 checks (spec 2.1) and CI runs it on every push. No new canary: `scripts/canaries.mjs` has 297 lines against the 300-line cap of `eslint.config.js:64`; the test proves each failure itself, and Task 2 plants a byte to see the gate go red.
- **W3 Ten pinned files**, every file the app's code and tests read: `design/brand/tokens.css`, eight files of `design/brand/logo/` (`metis-app-icon.svg`, `metis-app-icon-180.png`, `metis-app-icon-square.svg`, `metis-app-icon-square-1024.png`, `metis-app-icon-android-foreground.svg`, `metis-app-icon-android-foreground-1024.png`, `metis-favicon-48.png`, `metis-wordmark.svg`) and `design/wireframes/manifest.json`.
- **W4 `docs.lock` is JSON**: `{ "repository": "metis-docs", "commit": "none: metis-docs has no commit yet", "files": { "<metis-docs path>": "<sha256>" } }`, written by `hashesOf` of `scripts/pinned.mjs`. Plan two's bot rewrites the commit and the hashes, and its pull request must also rerun `pnpm gen:tokens` and refresh `assets/brand/` and `public/apple-touch-icon.png`, which `brand-files.test.mjs` compares with the copies.
- **W5 `gate:language` scans the repository root** and skips `.git` and `pinned/`: the copies are `metis-docs` files, checked there by its own rules (which allow dates and plan ids), and the app cannot edit them. The exemptions of `brand/style-guide.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` go, since both files leave the app.
- **W6 `.prettierignore` adds `pinned`.** Measured: Prettier flags both `brand/tokens.css` and `wireframes/manifest.json`, and at the root `prettier --check .` reaches every new top folder and `.github/`; formatting a copy would break its hash.
- **W7 The native gate leaves `.git` out of its copy**, now that the app folder is the repository root (its rsync used to copy only the app).
- **W8 `routes.test.ts` reads the manifest by a plain relative path.** StrykerJS 10 copies the working folder into its sandbox except `node_modules`, `.git` and its ignore patterns (`node_modules/@stryker-mutator/core/dist/src/fs/project-reader.js:9-17, 239-268`), so `pinned/` is there during mutation testing.
- **W9 The root `.gitignore` merges into the app's**: three rules it lacked (`.nx/`, `storybook-static/`, `*.local`); the list of files git would track is unchanged (425 before and after, measured). Each repository also ignores `.claude/settings.local.json`: Claude Code ignores that file by itself only when it wrote it [Source: code.claude.com/docs/en/settings, section "Keep personal settings out of a repository"].
- **W10 Each code repository also gets a one-line `CLAUDE.md`** (`@AGENTS.md`). Claude Code reads `AGENTS.md` by default only when no `CLAUDE.md` exists in the working folder or above it [Source: code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, section "When Claude Code reads AGENTS.md"], and the owner's workspace has `/Users/mrpo/projects/CLAUDE.md` above any clone under `~/projects`. Spec 6.1 names README and AGENTS only, so this is listed in Open questions too.
- **W11 The BRD build after the move.** `build.py` gains `--md-only`, `--out` and `--ids`; it reads the legacy text from `history/brd/legacy/` and the wireframes from `design/wireframes/`; the `sips` crop is gone because the 15 cropped POC images move with the source (`source/images/`; the five `poc-NN 2.jpg` files are byte copies of their originals and stay behind); `reference.docx` is built in the temporary folder for both documents and not committed; the main BRD's Word footer says v4.5 (it said v4.3, the default of `make_ref.py`); an en dash now fails both builds. The Markdown edition needs Python only, so it builds on Linux.
- **W12 Dashes.** The 65 en dashes of the BRD parts are all tight ranges (`M01` to `M12`, `1` to `18`), 23 of them POC ranges that `build.py` parses with a hyphen already, so each becomes a hyphen. The English records (four archived BRDs, the legacy text) get the same mechanical hyphen for both dashes; the Vietnamese records lose theirs in translation.
- **W13 A page is a Markdown file**, except the root `CLAUDE.md` (one import line, spec 3.5) and the BRD parts under `business/requirements/source/**/parts/`, which are fragments of the generated BRD. Spec 3.3 says every file carries the header and 3.6 checks every page; HTML, CSS, JSON, SVG and images cannot carry YAML, so the header rule applies to pages.
- **W14 Header syntax.** The fields of 3.3 in its order; `title` and `summary` are plain YAML text, or a JSON string in double quotes when they hold a colon; `generated_from` names a file of this repository for a page generated inside `metis-docs` (no commit: the same commit holds both) and `<repository>/<path>@<commit>` across repositories.
- **W15 Ids.** Header `ids` hold BRD ids, which `build.py --ids` lists (431 today). In the text of a current page that is not generated, every token shaped like a BRD id must exist, and every "screen N" must be in the wireframe manifest. Records are not searched (they cite older BRD versions) and record headers carry `ids: []`. Command names join the rule when the core's catalog exists (plan two).
- **W16 Links.** Markdown links and images outside code; the file must exist inside the repository; an `#anchor` must match a heading by GitHub's rule (all 170 table-of-contents anchors of the two BRD editions pass). A link to a folder resolves when the folder holds a file.
- **W17 The English check** is the app's letter rule with its `lang-exception:` line, not the app's reference rules: dates, plan ids and spec sections are normal in documents.
- **W18 The dash check** covers every text file (a file is binary when it holds a NUL byte or is not UTF-8), with no exception.
- **W19 Generated files** compared by the check: `llms.txt`, every record banner, the two BRD Markdown editions, and the wireframe `manifest.json`, `index.html` and `wireframes-digest.md` (`build-index.mjs` takes the date from `WIREFRAMES_DATE`; the committed date `2026-10-03` reproduces the manifest and the gallery byte for byte). Not compared: the logo and wireframe PNGs, rendered by Chrome and not byte-reproducible.
- **W20 Record banners** come from `history/records.json`: `written` is the last-modified date of the source file measured on 11 Oct 2026, `replacedBy` the current pages that now carry its lasting content, `translation` one of `whole`, `passages` or `none`. The banner sits right after the header, between two HTML comments.
- **W21 `llms.txt` (R5).** Sections: Start (the root pages), then business, design, architecture, components, operations, proposals, tools, any other folder by name, and Optional last. A draft page stays in its folder's section, its line starting `Draft.` before the summary, so an agent sees what is planned without mistaking it for built. Records and superseded pages are listed only under Optional.
- **W22 Secret scan:** gitleaks 8.30.1, in CI as the release tarball checked against its sha256 (`551f6fc83ea457d62a0d98237cbad105af8d557003051f41f3e7ca7b3f2470eb`, read from the release's checksum file and verified on the downloaded file), not the gitleaks GitHub Action, whose terms for organizations are [Unverified - confirm before applying]. Today's files: 0 findings.
- **W23 Translation line for line.** A translation keeps the line count; every line that holds no letter outside ASCII and no dash stays byte for byte; a heading keeps its level and a table row its cells. Proven on the 78-line plan of 9 Oct 2026. The 20,046-line plan of 6 Oct is cut at headings outside code into 13 chunks of at most 2,000 lines (the largest holds 785 Vietnamese lines), one subagent each, joined with `cat` (the joined chunks equal the file byte for byte); the 4,381-line plan of 5 Oct into 3 chunks.
- **W24 Translated passages of English files.** A record says so in its banner (`translation: passages`); the spec in `proposals/` has no banner, so each line whose Vietnamese was translated ends with `(machine translation)`.
- **W25 The archived BRD versions** linked their POC images, logo and figures from `brd/`; after the move those 107 links point to the copies `metis-docs` keeps, and all resolve.
- **W26 Layout of `history/`:** `brd/archive/` (BRD v4.1 to v4.4, addendum v1.0), `brd/legacy/`, `brd/addendum-onboarding/` (design, rulings, plan, option catalogue, research), `plans/` (the five plans from 5 Oct 2026, and this plan when it ships), `specs/` (the frontend spec of 5 Oct, the cross-platform research, the frontend decision log), `code-review/` (today's `analysis/metis-code-review/`), `reviews/` (today's `review/*.md`).
- **W27 Decision records.** A decision the owner took is `current`; a proposal the owner has not chosen is `draft`; a replaced one is `superseded`. The owner's working rules (FE-18, FE-21, FE-23) are records too, with `component: all`.
- **W28 The style guide** becomes an English current page of sections 1 to 9: section 10 (the version history) and the version line go, because a current page tells no "changed on" story (3.4) and the BRD review dispositions in `history/reviews/` keep what each version changed. The Greek capital delta of lines 118 and 131 (U+0394, a letter the English check rejects) is written "delta E".
- **W29 The voided backend findings.** `review/brd-findings-backend.md` moves to `history/reviews/` as a record whose banner names no current page: the owner voided it with the old backend log on 9 Oct 2026 (`spec/2026-10-09-backend-brainstorm-log.md:7`), so none of its content is carried into current pages.
- **W30 `develop.md` keeps no Vietnamese:** the one sample line of `CONTRIBUTING.md:18` names "a project name typed with Vietnamese letters" instead of quoting one.
- **W31 The docs tools need nothing installed:** plain Node modules with `node --test`, 100% line, branch and function coverage like the app's `gate:tooling`, and no `package.json`.
- **W32 The migration tools stay outside every repository** (`~/metis-run/repos-tools/`): they compare with originals that stay in the owner's private store.

  roots.push(root)

    mkdirSync(dirname(join(root, PINNED, path)), { recursive: true })

  return root
}

- [ ] **Step 3: Write `scripts/pinned.mjs`:**

```js
// metis-docs is the source of the brand files and the wireframe manifest. The app reads copies under
// pinned/, and docs.lock names the sha256 of each one, so a copy edited by hand fails gate:tooling.
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join, relative } from 'node:path'

export const LOCK = 'docs.lock'
export const PINNED = 'pinned'

// The sha256 of every file under root/pinned, keyed by its path inside pinned/ and sorted by path.
// Finder's .DS_Store is no copy, and git ignores it.
export function hashesOf(root) {
  const dir = join(root, PINNED)
  const paths = readdirSync(dir, { recursive: true, withFileTypes: true })
    .filter((entry) => entry.isFile() && entry.name !== '.DS_Store')
    .map((entry) => relative(dir, join(entry.parentPath, entry.name)))
    .sort()
  const hash = (path) =>
    createHash('sha256')
      .update(readFileSync(join(dir, path)))
      .digest('hex')
  return Object.fromEntries(paths.map((path) => [path, hash(path)]))
}

// Each copy that differs from its hash in docs.lock, is missing, or is not listed there.
export function pinnedProblems(root) {
  const { files } = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, LOCK), 'utf8'))
  const hashes = hashesOf(root)
  const paths = [...new Set([...Object.keys(files), ...Object.keys(hashes)])].sort()
  return paths.flatMap((path) => {
    const copy = `${PINNED}/${path}`
    if (!Object.hasOwn(hashes, path)) return [`${copy} is missing`]
    if (!Object.hasOwn(files, path)) return [`${copy} is not in ${LOCK}`]
    return hashes[path] === files[path] ? [] : [`${copy} differs from ${LOCK}`]
  })
}
```

    ("package_json_file: apps/metis/package.json", "package_json_file: package.json"),
    ("cache-dependency-path: apps/metis/pnpm-lock.yaml", "cache-dependency-path: pnpm-lock.yaml"),
    ("path: apps/metis/reports/verify.md", "path: reports/verify.md"),
]

for name, pairs in EDITS.items():
    path = ROOT / name
    text = path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    for old, new in pairs:
        count = text.count(old)
        if count != 1:
            sys.exit(f'{name}: expected 1 match, found {count}: {old[:70]!r}')
        text = text.replace(old, new)
    if name == '.github/workflows/check.yml':
        for old, new in PER_JOB:
            count = text.count(old)
            if count != 3:
                sys.exit(f'{name}: expected 3 matches, found {count}: {old!r}')
            text = text.replace(old, new)
        if 'apps/metis' in text:
            sys.exit(f'{name}: still names apps/metis')
    path.write_text(text, encoding='utf-8')
    print(f'edited {name}')
```

```markdown
# metis-app

The Metis app: one Expo code base and three builds, web, iOS and Android.

Its documentation lives in the `metis-docs` repository, under `components/app/`: start with
`README.md` there, then `develop.md` for building, running and testing the app.

## Quick start

1. Node 24.15.0 (`.nvmrc`) and pnpm 11.28.4 (`packageManager` in `package.json`).
2. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
3. `pnpm web` opens the app in a browser with mock data.
4. `pnpm verify` runs the 13 checks and writes `reports/verify.md`.

## Pinned design files

`pinned/` holds copies of files whose source is `metis-docs`: the brand tokens and logos, and the
wireframe manifest. `docs.lock` names the sha256 of each copy, and `gate:tooling` fails when a copy
differs from it, so a change to these files starts in `metis-docs`.
```

- [ ] **Step 1: Write `~/metis-run/repos-tools/docs_move.sh`:**

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Copies every file that moves into metis-docs from today's folder (read-only) into the working tree.
# Usage: sh docs_move.sh <today's folder> <metis-docs working tree>
set -eu
SRC=$1
DOCS=$2
LIST=$(mktemp)
# Copies the files git would track under one source folder, keeping their paths below it.
move() {
  from=$1
  to=$2
  shift 2
  git -C "$SRC" ls-files -co --exclude-standard -- "$from" | sed "s#^$from/##" > "$LIST"
  for skip in "$@"; do
    grep -v -e "$skip" "$LIST" > "$LIST.kept" || true
    mv "$LIST.kept" "$LIST"
  done
  mkdir -p "$DOCS/$to"
  rsync -a --files-from="$LIST" "$SRC/$from/" "$DOCS/$to/"
}
# Copies one file to a new path.
one() {
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$DOCS/$2")"
  cp "$SRC/$1" "$DOCS/$2"
}

# Design: the brand files and the wireframes; the style guide is translated by its own task.
move brand design/brand '^style-guide\.md$'
move wireframes design/wireframes

# The requirements source: parts, build scripts and evidence; records go to history below.
REQ=business/requirements/source
for f in README.md build.py make_ref.py evidence.tsv; do one "brd/source/$f" "$REQ/$f"; done
move brd/source/parts "$REQ/parts"
move brd/source/addendum-onboarding/parts "$REQ/addendum-onboarding/parts"
one brd/source/addendum-onboarding/evidence.tsv "$REQ/addendum-onboarding/evidence.tsv"
# The cropped POC screenshots the BRD shows; the five copies named "poc-NN 2.jpg" are byte duplicates.
move brd/images "$REQ/images" ' 2\.jpg$'

# Records: old BRD versions, the legacy BRD text, the addendum's working files.
move brd/archive history/brd/archive '\.docx$'
move brd/source/legacy history/brd/legacy
for f in 2026-10-02-onboarding-design.md 2026-10-03-execution-rulings.md \
  2026-10-03-onboarding-addendum-plan.md option-catalogue.md; do
  one "brd/source/addendum-onboarding/$f" "history/brd/addendum-onboarding/$f"
done
move brd/source/addendum-onboarding/research history/brd/addendum-onboarding/research

# Records: the delivered frontend plans, their spec and log, the code review, the BRD reviews.
for f in 2026-10-05-frontend-foundation.md 2026-10-06-frontend-overview-screen.md \
  2026-10-09-frontend-narrow-widths.md 2026-10-09-frontend-trace-and-gaps.md \
  2026-10-10-frontend-code-cleanup.md; do
  one "plan/$f" "history/plans/$f"
done
for f in 2026-10-05-frontend-foundation-spec.md 2026-10-05-cross-platform-research.md \
  frontend-brainstorm-log.md; do
  one "spec/$f" "history/specs/$f"
done
move analysis/metis-code-review history/code-review
git -C "$SRC" ls-files -co --exclude-standard -- 'review/*.md' | while read -r f; do
  one "$f" "history/reviews/$(basename "$f")"
done

# The approved design of this work, and the app's conventions page.
one spec/2026-10-11-repos-and-docs-design.md proposals/2026-10-11-repos-and-docs-design.md
one apps/metis/CONTRIBUTING.md components/app/develop.md
rm -f "$LIST"
```

    ("""REF = HERE / "reference.docx" if MAIN else tmp / "reference.docx"
subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(HERE / "make_ref.py")] + ([] if MAIN else [FOOTER, str(REF)]), check=True, capture_output=True)""",
     """REF = tmp / "reference.docx"
subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(HERE / "make_ref.py"), FOOTER, str(REF)], check=True, capture_output=True)"""),
]
# pandoc reads the parts' links from the folder of the Markdown edition, business/requirements.
PANDOC = ('"--resource-path", str(BRD)], check=True, cwd=BRD)', '"--resource-path", str(REQ)], check=True, cwd=REQ)')

PARTS = [
    # The images and the logo are linked from the Markdown edition, which sits in business/requirements.
    ('](images/poc-', '](source/images/poc-'),
    ('![](../brand/logo/metis-wordmark@2x.png)', '![](../../design/brand/logo/metis-wordmark@2x.png)'),
]


def edit(path, pairs, exact=True):
    text = path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    for old, new in pairs:
        count = text.count(old)
        if exact and count != 1:
            sys.exit(f'{path}: expected 1 match, found {count}: {old[:70]!r}')
        text = text.replace(old, new)
    return text


build = SOURCE / 'build.py'
text = edit(build, BUILD)
if text.count(PANDOC[0]) != 2:
    sys.exit(f'{build}: expected the pandoc call twice')
build.write_text(text.replace(PANDOC[0], PANDOC[1]), encoding='utf-8')
print(f'edited {build.relative_to(ROOT)}')

# The en dash of a range becomes a hyphen, which the POC range reader of build.py already accepts.
for part in sorted(SOURCE.glob('parts/*.md')) + sorted(SOURCE.glob('addendum-onboarding/parts/*.md')):
    text = part.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    new = text.replace('\u2013', '-')
    for old, repl in PARTS:
        new = new.replace(old, repl)
    if new != text:
        part.write_text(new, encoding='utf-8')
        print(f'edited {part.relative_to(ROOT)}')
```

# The BRD editions built in metis-docs equal the committed ones of today's folder plus the moves only:
# the page header, hyphens for en dashes, and the image, logo and figure paths of the new layout.
# Usage: python3 brd_md_oracle.py <today's folder> <metis-docs working tree>
import sys
from pathlib import Path

TODAY, DOCS = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2])
HEADER = ('---\ntitle: {}\nsummary: {}\ncomponent: all\ntype: reference\nstatus: current\nids: []\n'
          'generated_from: business/requirements/source/build.py\n---\n\n')
EDITIONS = [
    ('Enterprise_Portfolio_Intelligence_Governance_Platform_BRD_v4.5.md', 'BRD v4.5',
     'The business requirements of Metis, generated from source/parts by build.py.'),
    ('Enterprise_Portfolio_Intelligence_Governance_Platform_BRD_Addendum_Onboarding_v1.1.md', 'BRD addendum, onboarding v1.1',
     'The onboarding addendum to BRD v4.5, generated from source/addendum-onboarding by build.py.'),
]
failed = 0
for name, title, summary in EDITIONS:
    text = (TODAY / 'brd' / name).read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    for old, new in [('\u2013', '-'), ('](images/poc-', '](source/images/poc-'),
                     ('](../brand/logo/', '](../../design/brand/logo/'), ('](../wireframes/', '](../../design/wireframes/')]:
        text = text.replace(old, new)
    same = HEADER.format(title, summary) + text == (DOCS / 'business/requirements' / name).read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    failed += not same
    print(f"{name}: {'equal to the committed edition after the moves' if same else 'DIFFERENT'}")
sys.exit(1 if failed else 0)

### Task 7: The checks of metis-docs (spec 3.5, 3.6, W13 to W22)

**Files:**
- Create: `tools/docs.mjs`, `tools/check.mjs`, `tools/generate.mjs`, `tools/docs.test.mjs`, `tools/check.test.mjs`, `.github/workflows/check.yml`, `.gitignore`, `.nvmrc`, `CLAUDE.md`

**Interfaces:**
- `node tools/check.mjs [root]`: one line per problem, `path:line: rule: message`, rules `header`, `id`, `link`, `non-ascii-letter`, `dash`, `generated`, `record`; last line `check: clean (<pages> pages, <files> files)` and exit 0, or `check: <n> problems` and exit 1.
- `node tools/generate.mjs [root]`: writes `llms.txt` and every record banner; last line `generate: wrote llms.txt and <n> record banners`.
- `tools/docs.mjs` exports the checks (`headerOf`, `headerProblems`, `idProblems`, `linkProblems`, `languageProblems`, `dashProblems`), the generators (`llmsOf`, `bannerOf`, `withBanner`, `recordsOf`) and `repositoryOf`, which Task 8's oracles import.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests** `tools/docs.test.mjs` and `tools/check.test.mjs`:

````js
// Tests of the checks and generators of tools/docs.mjs, run with node --test.
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path'
import { after, test } from 'node:test'

import {
  anchorsOf,
  BANNER_END,
  BANNER_START,
  bannerOf,
  dashProblems,
  filesOf,
  headerOf,
  headerProblems,
  idProblems,
  isPage,
  languageProblems,
  linkProblems,
  linksOf,
  LLMS_NOTE,
  LLMS_SUMMARY,
  LLMS_TITLE,
  llmsOf,
  RECORDS,
  recordsOf,
  repositoryOf,
  textOf,
  withBanner
} from './docs.mjs'

// Letters and dashes the checks reject, written as escapes so that this file passes them.
const ACCENTED = 'Caf\u00e9'
const VIETNAMESE = 'Ti\u1ebfng Vi\u1ec7t'
const EN_DASH = '\u2013'
const EM_DASH = '\u2014'

const HEAD = {
  title: 'Change request',
  summary: 'How a change request goes from logged to applied.',
  component: 'all',
  type: 'journey',
  status: 'current',
  ids: ['CHG-01', 'BR-42']
}
// The header lines of a page, from a header object as headerOf returns it.
const headerText = (header) =>
  [
    '---',
    ...Object.entries(header).map(([key, value]) =>
      Array.isArray(value) ? `${key}: [${value.join(', ')}]` : `${key}: ${value}`
    ),
    '---'
  ].join('\n')
const page = (header = HEAD, body = '# Title\n') => `${headerText(header)}\n\n${body}`

const roots = []
// A temporary repository holding the given files, removed when this file's tests end.
const repository = (files) => {
  const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'docs-'))
  roots.push(root)
  for (const [path, text] of Object.entries(files)) {
    mkdirSync(dirname(join(root, path)), { recursive: true })
    writeFileSync(join(root, path), text)
  }
  return root
}
after(() => roots.forEach((root) => rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true })))

  assert.deepEqual(filesOf(root), ['a/c.md', 'b.md'])
})

  assert.equal(textOf(Buffer.from([0xff, 0xfe, 0x41])), null)
})

    [`${headerText(HEAD).slice(0, -4)}\nowner: me\n---\n`, 'the header must end with --- after its fields', 8]
  ]
  for (const [text, problem, line] of cases) assert.deepEqual(headerOf(text), { problem, line }, problem)

test('headerProblems keeps records in history/ and checks where generated_from points', () => {

  assert.deepEqual(headerProblems('history/a.md', { ...HEAD, type: 'record' }, exists), [

  const once = withBanner(text, 8, 'B1')
  assert.equal(once, `${headerText(HEAD)}\n\nB1\n\n# Body\n`)
  const old = `${headerText(HEAD)}\n\n${BANNER_START}\nold\n${BANNER_END}\n\n# Body\n`
  assert.equal(withBanner(old, 8, 'B2'), `${headerText(HEAD)}\n\nB2\n\n# Body\n`)
  const broken = `${headerText(HEAD)}\n${BANNER_START}\n# Body\n`
  assert.equal(withBanner(broken, 8, 'B3'), `${headerText(HEAD)}\n\nB3\n\n# Body\n`)
})

test('repositoryOf reads pages with their headers and gives null for a missing file', () => {
  const root = repository({ 'a.md': page(), 'b.md': '# no header\n', 'c/d.png': '\0' })
  const repo = repositoryOf(root)
  assert.deepEqual(repo.files, ['a.md', 'b.md', 'c/d.png'])
  assert.equal(repo.exists('c'), true)
  assert.equal(repo.exists('e'), false)
  assert.equal(repo.read('c/d.png'), null)
  assert.equal(repo.read('none.md'), null)
  assert.equal(repo.read('a.md'), repo.read('a.md'))
  assert.deepEqual(
    repo.pages.map(({ path, header, problem }) => [path, header?.title, problem]),
    [
      ['a.md', HEAD.title, undefined],
      ['b.md', undefined, 'no header: the first line must be ---']
    ]
  )
})

test('recordsOf builds each banner from the table and reports where table and pages disagree', () => {
  const record = { ...HEAD, title: 'Old plan', type: 'record', status: 'record' }
  const root = repository({
    'components/app/develop.md': page({ ...HEAD, title: 'Develop the app' }),
    'history/plans/p.md': page(record, '# Plan\n'),
    'history/plans/q.md': page(record, '# Plan Q\n'),
    [RECORDS]: JSON.stringify({
      'history/plans/p.md': { written: '2026-10-05', replacedBy: ['components/app/develop.md', 'none.md'], translation: 'none' },
      'history/plans/gone.md': { written: '2026-10-05', replacedBy: ['history/plans/q.md'], translation: 'french' }
    })
  })
  const { expected, problems } = recordsOf(repositoryOf(root))
  assert.deepEqual([...expected.keys()], ['history/plans/p.md'])
  // A replacing page that does not exist keeps its path as its title, and is reported.
  assert.match(
    expected.get('history/plans/p.md'),
    /Replaced by \[Develop the app\]\(\.\.\/\.\.\/components\/app\/develop\.md\), \[none\.md\]\(\.\.\/\.\.\/none\.md\)\./
  )
  assert.deepEqual(problems, [
    `history/plans/q.md:1: record: no entry in ${RECORDS}`,
    `${RECORDS}:1: record: history/plans/p.md is replaced by none.md, which is no current page`,
    `${RECORDS}:1: record: history/plans/gone.md is no record page`,
    `${RECORDS}:1: record: history/plans/gone.md has translation french, not whole, passages or none`,
    `${RECORDS}:1: record: history/plans/gone.md is replaced by history/plans/q.md, which is no current page`
  ])
  assert.deepEqual(recordsOf(repositoryOf(repository({ 'a.md': page() }))), { expected: new Map(), problems: [] })
})

// Tests of tools/check.mjs and tools/generate.mjs on a small repository, run with node --test. Its
// build.py and build-index.mjs are stand-ins that write fixed outputs, so the tests need no BRD.
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path'
import { after, test } from 'node:test'

import { BRD_DOCS, BUILD, check, WIREFRAMES } from './check.mjs'
import { RECORDS } from './docs.mjs'
import { generate } from './generate.mjs'

const VIETNAMESE = 'Ti\u1ebfng Vi\u1ec7t'
const EM_DASH = '\u2014'
const BRD_IDS = ['OVW-01', 'BR-24']
const DATE = '2026-10-03'

const header = (title, type = 'overview', status = 'current', extra = '') =>
  `---\ntitle: ${title}\nsummary: About ${title}.\ncomponent: all\ntype: ${type}\nstatus: ${status}\nids: []\n${extra}---\n\n# ${title}\n`
const generatedPage = (title, from) => header(title, 'reference', 'current', `generated_from: ${from}\n`)

// The stand-in build.py: --ids lists the ids; a document writes <doc>.md into --out. A file named
// FAIL beside it makes a document fail, and FAIL_IDS makes --ids fail.
const BUILD_PY = `import pathlib, sys
here = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent
args = sys.argv[1:]
if args == ["--ids"]:
    if (here / "FAIL_IDS").exists():
        sys.exit("ids failed")
    print("\\n".join(${JSON.stringify(BRD_IDS)}))
    sys.exit(0)
if (here / "FAIL").exists():
    sys.exit("build failed")
out = pathlib.Path(args[args.index("--out") + 1])
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
(out / (args[0] + ".md")).write_text(${JSON.stringify(generatedPage('BRD', BUILD))})
`
const BUILDER = `${WIREFRAMES}/tools/build-index.mjs`
const DIGEST = generatedPage('Digest', BUILDER)
// The stand-in build-index.mjs writes its three outputs with the date it is given.
const BUILD_INDEX = `import { existsSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
if (existsSync('FAIL')) process.exit(1)
const date = process.env.WIREFRAMES_DATE
writeFileSync('manifest.json', JSON.stringify({ generated: date, screens: [{ order: 24 }] }) + '\\n')
writeFileSync('index.html', '<p>' + date + '</p>\\n')
writeFileSync('wireframes-digest.md', ${JSON.stringify(DIGEST)})
`
const RECORD = 'history/plans/p.md'
const OVERVIEW = 'business/overview.md'

const roots = []
after(() => roots.forEach((root) => rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true })))
const write = (root, path, text) => {
  mkdirSync(dirname(join(root, path)), { recursive: true })
  writeFileSync(join(root, path), text)
}
// A complete small repository, with llms.txt and the record banner generated.
const repository = () => {
  const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'check-'))
  roots.push(root)
  const files = {
    'CLAUDE.md': '@AGENTS.md\n',
    'README.md': header('Readme'),
    [OVERVIEW]: `${header('Overview').replace('ids: []', `ids: [${BRD_IDS[0]}]`)}\n${BRD_IDS[1]} on screen 24, see [the readme](../README.md).\n`,
    [RECORD]: header('Old plan', 'record', 'record'),
    [RECORDS]: JSON.stringify({ [RECORD]: { written: '2026-10-05', replacedBy: [OVERVIEW], translation: 'whole' } }),
    [BUILD]: BUILD_PY,
    ...Object.fromEntries(BRD_DOCS.map((doc) => [`business/requirements/${doc}.md`, generatedPage('BRD', BUILD)])),
    [`${WIREFRAMES}/manifest.json`]: `${JSON.stringify({ generated: DATE, screens: [{ order: 24 }] })}\n`,
    [`${WIREFRAMES}/index.html`]: `<p>${DATE}</p>\n`,
    [`${WIREFRAMES}/wireframes-digest.md`]: DIGEST,
    [BUILDER]: BUILD_INDEX,
    'design/brand/logo.png': Buffer.from([0x89, 0x50, 0x00])
  }
  for (const [path, text] of Object.entries(files)) write(root, path, text)
  assert.deepEqual(generate(root), { banners: 1, problems: [] })
  return { root, paths: Object.keys(files) }
}
const edit = (root, path, change) => write(root, path, change(readFileSync(join(root, path), 'utf8')))
// Appends one line to a file and returns its line number.
const append = (root, path, line) => {
  const at = readFileSync(join(root, path), 'utf8').split('\n').length
  edit(root, path, (text) => `${text}${line}\n`)
  return at
}

test('a complete repository is clean, and generate wrote llms.txt and the banner of each record', () => {
  const { root, paths } = repository()
  // Every file of the repository plus the generated llms.txt; every Markdown file but CLAUDE.md is a page.
  const pages = paths.filter((path) => path.endsWith('.md') && path !== 'CLAUDE.md').length
  assert.deepEqual(check(root), { problems: [], files: paths.length + 1, pages })
  assert.match(readFileSync(join(root, 'llms.txt'), 'utf8'), /^- \[Old plan\]\(history\/plans\/p\.md\): About Old plan\.$/m)
  assert.match(readFileSync(join(root, RECORD), 'utf8'), /machine translation of a Vietnamese record/)
})

test('each rule names the file, the line and what is wrong', () => {
  const { root } = repository()
  const readme = append(root, 'README.md', `${VIETNAMESE} ${EM_DASH}`)
  const overview = append(root, OVERVIEW, 'OVW-09 and [gone](gone.md)')
  write(root, 'business/plain.md', '# No header\n')
  write(root, 'business/old.md', header('Old', 'record', 'record'))
  const { problems } = check(root)
  const expected = [
    `README.md:${readme}: non-ascii-letter: ${VIETNAMESE} ${EM_DASH}`,
    `README.md:${readme}: dash: ${VIETNAMESE} ${EM_DASH}`,
    `${OVERVIEW}:${overview}: id: OVW-09 is no BRD id`,
    `${OVERVIEW}:${overview}: link: gone.md: no such file`,
    'business/old.md:1: header: only a page under history/ is a record',
    'business/plain.md:1: header: no header: the first line must be ---',
    'llms.txt:1: generated: not what tools/generate.mjs writes now'
  ]
  assert.deepEqual([...problems].sort(), [...expected].sort())
})

test('a generated file that differs from what its generator writes now is a problem', () => {
  const { root } = repository()
  edit(root, 'llms.txt', (text) => `${text}\n`)
  edit(root, RECORD, (text) => text.replace('It is never current truth.', 'It is the truth.'))
  edit(root, `business/requirements/${BRD_DOCS[0]}.md`, (text) => `${text}\n`)

  assert.deepEqual(check(root).problems, [

    `${RECORD}:1: generated: not what tools/generate.mjs writes now`,
    `business/requirements/${BRD_DOCS[0]}.md:1: generated: not what ${BUILD} ${BRD_DOCS[0]} writes now`,
    `${WIREFRAMES}/index.html:1: generated: not what ${BUILDER} writes now`

test('a builder that fails is a problem that quotes its output', () => {
  const { root } = repository()
  write(root, join(dirname(BUILD), 'FAIL'), '')
  write(root, join(dirname(BUILD), 'FAIL_IDS'), '')
  write(root, join(WIREFRAMES, 'FAIL'), '')
  const { problems } = check(root)
  assert.deepEqual(problems.filter((line) => line.includes('failed')), [

  assert.ok(problems.includes(`${OVERVIEW}:1: id: ${BRD_IDS[0]} is no BRD id`), problems.join('\n'))
})

````js
// The checks every pull request of metis-docs runs, and the generators of llms.txt and the record
// banners. tools/check.mjs and tools/generate.mjs run them over the repository.
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join, posix, relative, sep } from 'node:path'

export const COMPONENTS = ['app', 'core', 'mcp-gateway', 'agent', 'keycloak', 'sandbox', 'infra', 'all']
export const TYPES = [
  'overview',
  'module',
  'journey',
  'how-to',
  'reference',
  'runbook',
  'decision',
  'incident',
  'proposal',
  'record'
]
export const STATUSES = ['current', 'draft', 'superseded', 'record']
const FIELDS = ['title', 'summary', 'component', 'type', 'status', 'ids']
const CHOICES = { component: COMPONENTS, type: TYPES, status: STATUSES }
const SKIP_DIRS = new Set(['.git', 'node_modules'])

// Every file under root, as sorted paths with / separators.
export function filesOf(root) {
  return readdirSync(root, { recursive: true, withFileTypes: true })
    .filter((entry) => entry.isFile())
    .map((entry) => relative(root, join(entry.parentPath, entry.name)).split(sep).join('/'))
    .filter((path) => !path.split('/').some((part) => SKIP_DIRS.has(part)))
    .sort()
}

const UTF8 = new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true })
// The text of a file, or null for a binary one: a NUL byte, or bytes that are not UTF-8.
export function textOf(bytes) {
  if (bytes.includes(0)) return null
  try {
    return UTF8.decode(bytes)
  } catch {
    return null
  }
}

// A page is a Markdown file, but the BRD parts are fragments of the generated BRD, and CLAUDE.md is the
// one import line that hands Claude Code to AGENTS.md.
export const isPage = (path) =>
  path.endsWith('.md') &&
  path !== 'CLAUDE.md' &&
  !/^business\/requirements\/source\/(?:.+\/)?parts\//.test(path)

// Plain YAML text that stays valid YAML: no indicator first, no ": " or " #" inside, no ":" last.
const PLAIN = /^(?![-?:,[\]{}#&*!|>'"%@`])(?!.*(?:: | #))(?!.*:$)\S(?:.*\S)?$/
const ID_LIST = /^\[(?:[A-Za-z0-9][\w.-]*(?:, [A-Za-z0-9][\w.-]*)*)?\]$/
const OTHER_REPOSITORY = /^[\w.-]+\/[^@\s]+@[0-9a-f]{7,40}$/

// The value of a text field: plain text, or a JSON string in double quotes for text with a colon.
const textValue = (raw) => {
  if (!raw.startsWith('"')) return PLAIN.test(raw) ? raw : null
  try {
    const value = JSON.parse(raw)
    return typeof value === 'string' && value.trim() ? value : null
  } catch {
    return null
  }
}

const valueOf = (field, raw) => {
  if (CHOICES[field]) return CHOICES[field].includes(raw) ? raw : null
  if (field === 'ids') return ID_LIST.test(raw) ? raw.slice(1, -1).split(', ').filter(Boolean) : null
  return textValue(raw)
}

// The header of 3.3: its fields in order, between two --- lines; generated_from may follow ids.
export function headerOf(text) {
  const lines = text.split('\n')
  if (lines[0] !== '---') return { problem: 'no header: the first line must be ---', line: 1 }
  const header = {}
  const names = [...FIELDS, 'generated_from']
  let at = 1
  for (const name of names) {
    const match = lines[at]?.match(/^([a-z_]+): (.+)$/)
    if (name === 'generated_from' && match?.[1] !== name) break
    if (match?.[1] !== name) return { problem: `line ${at + 1} must hold the field ${name}`, line: at + 1 }
    const value = valueOf(name, match[2])
    if (value === null) return { problem: `${name} is not valid: ${match[2]}`, line: at + 1 }
    header[name] = value
    at += 1
  }
  if (lines[at] !== '---') return { problem: 'the header must end with --- after its fields', line: at + 1 }
  return { header, lines: at + 1 }
}

// The rules a header must keep beyond its own syntax.
export function headerProblems(path, header, exists) {
  const problems = []
  const inHistory = path.startsWith('history/')
  const record = header.type === 'record' || header.status === 'record'
  if (inHistory && !(header.type === 'record' && header.status === 'record')) {
    problems.push('a page under history/ has type record and status record')
  }
  if (!inHistory && record) problems.push('only a page under history/ is a record')
  const from = header.generated_from
  if (from !== undefined && !OTHER_REPOSITORY.test(from) && !exists(from)) {
    problems.push(`generated_from names no file of this repository and no <repository>/<path>@<commit>: ${from}`)
  }
  return problems
}

const FENCE = /^\s*(```|~~~)/
// The lines of a text outside fenced code blocks, as [line number, text] pairs.
const proseOf = (text) => {
  let fenced = false
  return text.split('\n').flatMap((line, i) => {
    if (FENCE.test(line)) {
      fenced = !fenced
      return []
    }
    return fenced ? [] : [[i + 1, line]]
  })
}

const INLINE_CODE = /`+[^`]*`+/g
const LINK = /!?\[[^\]]*\]\(\s*(?:<([^>\n]+)>|([^)\s]+))(?:\s+"[^"]*")?\s*\)/g
const DEFINITION = /^\s{0,3}\[[^\]]+\]:\s*<?([^\s>]+)>?/

// The link and image targets of a Markdown page outside code, each with its line.
export function linksOf(text) {
  return proseOf(text).flatMap(([line, raw]) => {
    const prose = raw.replace(INLINE_CODE, '')
    const targets = [...prose.matchAll(LINK)].map((match) => match[1] ?? match[2])
    const definition = prose.match(DEFINITION)
    if (definition) targets.push(definition[1])
    return targets.map((target) => ({ line, target }))
  })
}

// GitHub's anchor of each heading: lower case; letters, digits, spaces, hyphens and underscores kept;
// each space a hyphen; a repeated anchor numbered -1, -2.
export function anchorsOf(text) {
  const seen = new Map()
  return proseOf(text).flatMap(([, line]) => {
    const heading = line.match(/^#{1,6}\s+(.*?)\s*#*\s*$/)
    if (!heading) return []
    const words = heading[1]
      .replace(/!?\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]*\)/g, '$1')
      .replace(/<[^>]+>/g, '')
      .toLowerCase()
      .replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N}\p{M}_ -]/gu, '')
      .replace(/ /g, '-')
    const count = seen.get(words) ?? 0
    seen.set(words, count + 1)
    return [count === 0 ? words : `${words}-${count}`]
  })
}

const SCHEME = /^(?:[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:|\/\/)/i
const decoded = (text, decode) => {
  try {
    return decode(text)
  } catch {
    return null
  }
}

// Each link of a page whose file does not exist, leaves the repository, or names a missing heading.
// exists(path) and readPage(path) see the repository; a folder exists when it holds a file.
export function linkProblems(path, text, { exists, readPage }) {
  return linksOf(text).flatMap(({ line, target }) => {
    if (SCHEME.test(target)) return []
    const [file, fragment = ''] = target.split('#')
    const named = decoded(file, decodeURI)
    const anchor = decoded(fragment, decodeURIComponent)
    if (named === null || anchor === null) {
      return [{ line, rule: 'link', message: `${target} is not a valid address` }]
    }
    // A folder link may end with a slash; the folder is what must exist.
    const resolved = file
      ? posix
          .normalize(named.startsWith('/') ? named.slice(1) : posix.join(posix.dirname(path), named))
          .replace(/(.)\/$/, '$1')
      : path
    if (resolved === '..' || resolved.startsWith('../')) {
      return [{ line, rule: 'link', message: `${target} leaves the repository` }]
    }
    if (!exists(resolved)) return [{ line, rule: 'link', message: `${target}: no such file` }]
    if (!fragment || !resolved.endsWith('.md')) return []
    const anchors = anchorsOf(resolved === path ? text : readPage(resolved))
    return anchors.includes(anchor)
      ? []
      : [{ line, rule: 'link', message: `${target}: no heading with the anchor #${anchor}` }]
  })
}

const LETTER = /(?![\x00-\x7F])\p{L}/u
// English only, with the method of the app's check-language.mjs: a letter outside ASCII is a problem,
// except on the line after one that holds lang-exception: and a reason.
export function languageProblems(text) {
  const lines = text.normalize('NFC').split('\n')
  return lines.flatMap((line, i) => {
    const excused = i > 0 && lines[i - 1].includes('lang-exception:')
    return !excused && LETTER.test(line)
      ? [{ line: i + 1, rule: 'non-ascii-letter', message: line.trim().slice(0, 100) }]
      : []
  })
}

// No em dash and no en dash anywhere.
export function dashProblems(text) {
  return text.split('\n').flatMap((line, i) =>
    /[\u2013\u2014]/.test(line)
      ? [{ line: i + 1, rule: 'dash', message: line.trim().slice(0, 100) }]
      : []
  )
}

// Each id a page names that the BRD does not define, and each screen number the manifest lacks. The
// header ids are BRD ids. Records and generated pages are not searched for ids in their text: a record
// may name an id of an older BRD, and a generator checks its own output.
export function idProblems(path, text, header, { brd, screens }) {
  const unknown = header.ids.filter((id) => !brd.has(id))
  const problems = unknown.map((id) => ({ line: 1, rule: 'id', message: `${id} is no BRD id` }))
  if (path.startsWith('history/') || header.generated_from !== undefined || brd.size === 0) {
    return problems
  }
  const prefixes = [...new Set([...brd].map((id) => id.split('-')[0]))].sort().join('|')
  const named = new RegExp(`\\b(?:${prefixes})-\\d{2}\\b`, 'g')
  text.split('\n').forEach((line, i) => {
    for (const [id] of line.matchAll(named)) {
      if (!brd.has(id)) problems.push({ line: i + 1, rule: 'id', message: `${id} is no BRD id` })
    }
    for (const [, number] of line.matchAll(/\b[Ss]creens? (\d{1,3})\b/g)) {
      if (!screens.has(Number(number))) {
        problems.push({ line: i + 1, rule: 'id', message: `screen ${number} is not in the wireframe manifest` })
      }
    }
  })
  return problems
}

// The order of the sections of llms.txt; other top folders follow in name order.
const SECTIONS = ['business', 'design', 'architecture', 'components', 'operations', 'proposals', 'tools']
export const LLMS_TITLE = '# Metis documentation'
export const LLMS_SUMMARY =
  '> The single source of truth about Metis for the team building it and its AI agents: what the ' +
  'product does today and for whom, its design, its architecture, each component, and how to run it.'
export const LLMS_NOTE =
  'Generated from the page headers by tools/generate.mjs; never edit it by hand. Read AGENTS.md first. ' +
  'A draft page describes a part that is planned, not built. The Optional section lists records and ' +
  'replaced pages, which are never current truth.'

// llms.txt in the llmstxt.org format: one section per top folder, records and replaced pages under Optional.
export function llmsOf(pages) {
  const item = ({ path, header }) => {
    const note = header.status === 'draft' ? `Draft. ${header.summary}` : header.summary
    return `- [${header.title}](${path}): ${note}`
  }
  const optional = (page) => page.path.startsWith('history/') || page.header.status === 'superseded'
  const sectionOf = (path) => (path.includes('/') ? path.split('/')[0] : 'Start')
  const groups = new Map()
  // Code point order, the same on every machine.
  for (const page of [...pages].sort((a, b) => (a.path > b.path) - (a.path < b.path))) {
    const name = optional(page) ? 'Optional' : sectionOf(page.path)
    groups.set(name, [...(groups.get(name) ?? []), item(page)])
  }
  const rest = [...groups.keys()].filter((name) => !['Start', 'Optional', ...SECTIONS].includes(name))
  const order = ['Start', ...SECTIONS, ...rest.sort(), 'Optional'].filter((name) => groups.has(name))
  const sections = order.map((name) => [`## ${name}`, '', ...groups.get(name), ''].join('\n'))
  return [LLMS_TITLE, '', LLMS_SUMMARY, '', LLMS_NOTE, '', ...sections].join('\n')
}

export const BANNER_START = '<!-- record banner: generated by tools/generate.mjs from history/records.json -->'
export const BANNER_END = '<!-- end of record banner -->'
const MONTHS = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec']
const dateOf = (iso) => {
  const [year, month, day] = iso.split('-').map(Number)
  return `${day} ${MONTHS[month - 1]} ${year}`
}

// What the banner says of a record's language: translation is whole, passages or none.
const TRANSLATIONS = {
  whole: " This is a machine translation of a Vietnamese record; the original is kept in the owner's private store.",
  passages: " Its Vietnamese passages are machine translations; the original is kept in the owner's private store.",
  none: ''
}

// The banner of a record: when it was written, the current pages that replaced it and, for a
// translation, where the original is. titleOf(path) reads a page's title.
export function bannerOf(path, record, titleOf) {
  const links = record.replacedBy.map(
    (page) => `[${titleOf(page)}](${posix.relative(posix.dirname(path), page)})`
  )
  const replaced = links.length
    ? `Replaced by ${links.join(', ')}.`
    : 'No current page replaces it.'
  const text = `> **Record, written ${dateOf(record.written)}.** It is never current truth. ${replaced}${TRANSLATIONS[record.translation]}`
  return [BANNER_START, text, BANNER_END].join('\n')
}

// The page with its banner right after the header, in place of an older banner.
export function withBanner(text, lines, banner) {
  const all = text.split('\n')
  const head = all.slice(0, lines)
  let body = all.slice(lines)
  const start = body.findIndex((line) => line === BANNER_START)
  if (start >= 0) {
    const end = body.indexOf(BANNER_END, start)
    body.splice(start, end < 0 ? 1 : end - start + 1)
  }
  while (body[0] === '') body = body.slice(1)
  return [...head, '', banner, '', ...body].join('\n')
}

export const RECORDS = 'history/records.json'

// The files of a repository, whether a path exists (a folder exists when it holds a file), a cached
// reader of text files, and its pages with their headers parsed.
export function repositoryOf(root) {
  const files = filesOf(root)
  const known = new Set(files.flatMap((file) => file.split('/').map((_, i, parts) => parts.slice(0, i + 1).join('/'))))
  const texts = new Map()
  const listed = new Set(files)
  // A missing file reads as null, like a binary one.
  const read = (path) => {
    if (!listed.has(path)) return null
    if (!texts.has(path)) texts.set(path, textOf(readFileSync(join(root, path))))
    return texts.get(path)
  }
  const pages = files.filter(isPage).map((path) => ({ path, text: read(path), ...headerOf(read(path)) }))
  return { files, exists: (path) => known.has(path), read, pages }
}

// The text each record page should have, its banner made from history/records.json, and every place
// where that table and the pages disagree.
export function recordsOf({ exists, read, pages }) {
  const problems = []
  const records = pages.filter((page) => page.path.startsWith('history/') && page.header)
  const table = exists(RECORDS) ? JSON.parse(read(RECORDS)) : {}
  const titles = new Map(pages.filter((page) => page.header).map((page) => [page.path, page.header.title]))
  const expected = new Map()
  for (const page of records) {
    const record = table[page.path]
    if (!record) {
      problems.push(`${page.path}:1: record: no entry in ${RECORDS}`)
      continue
    }
    const titleOf = (path) => titles.get(path) ?? path
    expected.set(page.path, withBanner(page.text, page.lines, bannerOf(page.path, record, titleOf)))
  }
  for (const [path, record] of Object.entries(table)) {
    if (!records.some((page) => page.path === path)) {
      problems.push(`${RECORDS}:1: record: ${path} is no record page`)
    }
    if (!Object.hasOwn(TRANSLATIONS, record.translation)) {
      problems.push(`${RECORDS}:1: record: ${path} has translation ${record.translation}, not whole, passages or none`)
    }
    for (const page of record.replacedBy) {
      if (!titles.has(page) || page.startsWith('history/')) {
        problems.push(`${RECORDS}:1: record: ${path} is replaced by ${page}, which is no current page`)
      }
    }
  }
  return { expected, problems }
}
````

```js
// node tools/check.mjs: every check of metis-docs over the repository, one line per problem as
// path:line: rule: message, and exit 1 when there is any. The secret scan runs apart, with gitleaks.
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { cpSync, mkdtempSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, realpathSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs'
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'

import {
  dashProblems,
  headerProblems,
  idProblems,
  languageProblems,
  linkProblems,
  llmsOf,
  recordsOf,
  repositoryOf
} from './docs.mjs'

// The documents build.py writes: the main BRD and each addendum, by the name build.py takes.
export const BRD_DOCS = ['main', 'addendum-onboarding']
export const BUILD = 'business/requirements/source/build.py'
const REQUIREMENTS = 'business/requirements'
export const WIREFRAMES = 'design/wireframes'
const WIREFRAME_OUTPUTS = ['manifest.json', 'index.html', 'wireframes-digest.md']

export const spawn = (command, args, options) =>
  spawnSync(command, args, { encoding: 'utf8', ...options })
const failed = (result) =>
  `exit ${result.status}: ${`${result.stdout}${result.stderr}`.trim().slice(-300)}`

// A generated file is what its generator writes now: build.py for the BRD, build-index.mjs for the
// wireframes (with the date the committed manifest carries), and tools/generate.mjs for the rest.
function generatedProblems(root, repo, run) {
  const { read, pages } = repo
  const problems = []
  const stale = (path, generator) =>
    problems.push(`${path}:1: generated: not what ${generator} writes now`)
  if (read('llms.txt') !== llmsOf(pages.filter((page) => page.header))) {
    stale('llms.txt', 'tools/generate.mjs')
  }
  const records = recordsOf(repo)
  problems.push(...records.problems)
  for (const [path, text] of records.expected) {
    if (read(path) !== text) stale(path, 'tools/generate.mjs')
  }
  const out = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'metis-docs-check-'))
  try {
    for (const doc of BRD_DOCS) {
      const target = join(out, doc)
      const result = run('python3', [BUILD, doc, '--md-only', '--out', target], { cwd: root })
      if (result.status !== 0) {
        problems.push(`${BUILD}:1: generated: build.py ${doc} failed, ${failed(result)}`)
        continue
      }
      for (const name of readdirSync(target)) {
        const path = `${REQUIREMENTS}/${name}`
        if (read(path) !== readFileSync(join(target, name), 'utf8')) stale(path, `${BUILD} ${doc}`)
      }
    }
    const copy = join(out, 'wireframes')
    cpSync(join(root, WIREFRAMES), copy, { recursive: true })
    const { generated } = JSON.parse(read(`${WIREFRAMES}/manifest.json`))
    const env = { ...process.env, WIREFRAMES_DATE: generated }
    const result = run('node', ['tools/build-index.mjs'], { cwd: copy, env })
    const builder = `${WIREFRAMES}/tools/build-index.mjs`
    if (result.status !== 0) problems.push(`${builder}:1: generated: failed, ${failed(result)}`)
    else {
      for (const name of WIREFRAME_OUTPUTS) {
        const path = `${WIREFRAMES}/${name}`
        if (read(path) !== readFileSync(join(copy, name), 'utf8')) stale(path, builder)
      }
    }
  } finally {
    rmSync(out, { recursive: true, force: true })
  }
  return problems
}

// Every problem of the repository at root, and how many files and pages it read.
export function check(root, run = spawn) {
  const repo = repositoryOf(root)
  const { files, exists, read, pages } = repo
  const problems = []
  const add = (path, found) =>
    found.forEach(({ line, rule, message }) => problems.push(`${path}:${line}: ${rule}: ${message}`))
  for (const path of files) {
    const text = read(path)
    if (text === null) continue
    add(path, languageProblems(text))
    add(path, dashProblems(text))
  }
  const listed = run('python3', [BUILD, '--ids'], { cwd: root })
  if (listed.status !== 0) problems.push(`${BUILD}:1: id: build.py --ids failed, ${failed(listed)}`)
  const brd = new Set(listed.status === 0 ? listed.stdout.split('\n').filter(Boolean) : [])
  const manifest = JSON.parse(read(`${WIREFRAMES}/manifest.json`))
  const screens = new Set(manifest.screens.map((screen) => screen.order))
  for (const { path, text, header, problem, line } of pages) {
    if (problem) {
      add(path, [{ line, rule: 'header', message: problem }])
      continue
    }
    const rules = headerProblems(path, header, exists)
    add(path, rules.map((message) => ({ line: 1, rule: 'header', message })))
    add(path, idProblems(path, text, header, { brd, screens }))
    add(path, linkProblems(path, text, { exists, readPage: read }))
  }
  problems.push(...generatedProblems(root, repo, run))
  return { problems, files: files.length, pages: pages.length }
}

/* node:coverage disable */
// Command line only: CI and people run it; check.test.mjs runs check() itself.
if (process.argv[1] && realpathSync(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) {
  const root = process.argv[2] ?? join(import.meta.dirname, '..')
  const { problems, files, pages } = check(root)
  for (const line of problems) console.log(line)
  console.log(
    problems.length
      ? `check: ${problems.length} problems`
      : `check: clean (${pages} pages, ${files} files)`
  )
  process.exitCode = problems.length ? 1 : 0
}
/* node:coverage enable */
```

```js
// node tools/generate.mjs: writes llms.txt from the page headers and the banner of every record from
// history/records.json. The BRD has its own builder (business/requirements/source/build.py), and so do
// the wireframe outputs (design/wireframes/tools/build-index.mjs).
import { realpathSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'

import { llmsOf, recordsOf, repositoryOf } from './docs.mjs'

// Writes the generated files of the repository at root and returns the problems that kept a record
// from getting its banner.
export function generate(root) {
  const repo = repositoryOf(root)
  writeFileSync(join(root, 'llms.txt'), llmsOf(repo.pages.filter((page) => page.header)))
  const { expected, problems } = recordsOf(repo)
  for (const [path, text] of expected) writeFileSync(join(root, path), text)
  return { banners: expected.size, problems }
}

/* node:coverage disable */
// Command line only: people and the docs agent run it; generate.test.mjs runs generate() itself.
if (process.argv[1] && realpathSync(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) {
  const { banners, problems } = generate(process.argv[2] ?? join(import.meta.dirname, '..'))
  for (const line of problems) console.log(line)
  console.log(`generate: wrote llms.txt and ${banners} record banners`)
  process.exitCode = problems.length ? 1 : 0
}
/* node:coverage enable */
```

# Every pull request and every push to main runs the checks of metis-docs: the tests of tools/, every
# page check of tools/check.mjs, and a secret scan.
name: check

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

# The least GITHUB_TOKEN access: read the documents, write nothing.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc
      # The checks prove themselves first, every line and branch of tools/ covered.
      - run: node --test --experimental-test-coverage --test-coverage-lines=100 --test-coverage-branches=100 --test-coverage-functions=100 --test-coverage-exclude='**/*.test.*' 'tools/*.test.mjs'
      # build.py writes the Markdown edition of the BRD with Python 3 and its standard library only.
      - run: python3 --version
      - run: node tools/check.mjs
      # A pinned gitleaks release, verified by its sha256, scans every file for secrets.
      - name: secret scan
        run: |
          curl -sSfL -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/gitleaks.tar.gz" https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v8.30.1/gitleaks_8.30.1_linux_x64.tar.gz
          echo "551f6fc83ea457d62a0d98237cbad105af8d557003051f41f3e7ca7b3f2470eb  $RUNNER_TEMP/gitleaks.tar.gz" | sha256sum --check
          tar -xzf "$RUNNER_TEMP/gitleaks.tar.gz" -C "$RUNNER_TEMP" gitleaks
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/gitleaks" dir . --no-banner --redact
```
